'''Raman Parimala''' (born 21 November 1948)<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www.agnesscott.edu/lriddle/women/parimala.htm|title=Raman Parimala|last=Riddle|first=Larry|website=Biographies of Young Women Mathematicians|publisher=Agnes Scott College|access-date=2016-03-23}}</ref> is an Indian [[mathematician]] known for her contributions to [[algebra]].  She is the Arts & Sciences Distinguished Professor of [[mathematics]] at [[Emory University]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.mathcs.emory.edu/faculty.php|title=Math/CS|website=www.mathcs.emory.edu|access-date=2016-03-23|archive-date=25 November 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181125073953/http://www.mathcs.emory.edu/faculty.php|url-status=dead}}</ref> For many years, she was a professor at [[Tata Institute of Fundamental Research]] (TIFR), [[Mumbai]]. 

She was on the Mathematical Sciences jury for the [[Infosys Prize]] 2019—2022<ref>{{Cite web|title=Infosys Prize - Jury 2020|url=http://www.infosys-science-foundation.com/prize/jury/jury-2020.asp|access-date=2020-12-10|website=www.infosys-science-foundation.com}}</ref> and was on the [[Abel Prize]] selection Committee 2021–2023.<ref>[https://www.abelprize.no/c53678/artikkel/vis.html?tid=53708 The Abel Committee 2021/2022] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190619220511/https://www.abelprize.no/c53678/artikkel/vis.html?tid=53708 |date=19 June 2019 }} The Abel Prize</ref>

== Background ==
Parimala was born and raised in [[Tamil Nadu]], India.<ref>{{Cite journal|date=September 2015|title=Biographies of Candidates 2015|url=https://www.ams.org/notices/201508/rnoti-p931a.pdf|journal=Notices of the AMS|publisher=American Mathematical Society|volume=62|issue=8|page=940|access-date=23 March 2016}}</ref> She studied in Saradha Vidyalaya Girls' High School and Stella Maris College at [[Chennai]]. She received her B. Sc. in 1968 and her M.Sc. in 1970 from [[Madras University]]. In 1976, Parimala earned her Ph.D. from the
[[University of Mumbai]]; her advisor was [[R. Sridharan]] from TIFR.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.genealogy.ams.org/id.php?id=59460|title=The Mathematics Genealogy Project - Raman Parimala|website=www.genealogy.ams.org|access-date=2016-03-23}}</ref>

In 1987, she won the highest science award in India: The [[Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize for Science and Technology|Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Sci-Illustrate |date=2021-01-12 |title=Raman Parimala |url=https://medium.com/sci-illustrate-stories/raman-parimala-6c345d4f528e |access-date=2024-02-22 |website=Sci-Illustrate Stories |language=en}}</ref>

She is a fellow of the Indian National Science Academy (New Delhi).<ref name=":1" />

== Selected publications ==
* 2021: "Local triviality for G-torsors", Gille, P.; Parimala, R.; Suresh, V., Math. Ann. 380, no. 1-2, 539–567. {{mr|4263691}}
* 2018: "Local-global principle for reduced norms over function fields of p-adic curves", Parimala, R.; Preeti, R.; Suresh, V., Compos. Math. 154, no. 2, 410–458. {{mr|3732207}}
* 2014: "Period-index and u-invariant questions for function fields over complete discretely valued fields", Parimala, R.; Suresh, V., Invent. Math. 197, no. 1, 215–235. {{mr|3219517}}
* 2001: "Hermitian analogue of a theorem of Springer", R Parimala, [[R. Sridharan]], V Suresh - Journal of Algebra, - Elsevier {{doi|10.1006/jabr.2001.8830}}
* 1998: "Classical groups and the Hasse principle", [[Eva Bayer-Fluckiger|E Bayer-Fluckiger]], R Parimala - Annals of Mathematics,  jstor.org<ref>[https://scholar.google.com/scholar?hl=en&lr=&q=%22R++Parimala%22&btnG=Search Google scholar]</ref> {{doi|10.2307/120961}}
* 1995: "Galois cohomology of the classical groups over fields of cohomological dimension ≤2", Bayer-Fluckiger, E.; Parimala, R., Invent. Math. 122, no. 2, 195–229. {{mr|1358975}}
* 1990: "Real components of algebraic varieties and étale cohomology", [[Jean-Louis Colliot-Thélène|Colliot-Thélène, J.-L.]]; Parimala, R., Invent. Math. 101, no. 1, 81–99. {{mr|1055712}}
* 1982: "Quadratic spaces over polynomial extensions of regular rings of dimension 2", Mathematische Annalen, vol. 261, pp.&nbsp;287–292 {{doi|10.1007/BF01455449}}
* 1976: "Failure of a quadratic analogue of Serre's conjecture", Bulletin of the AMS, vol. 82, pp.&nbsp;962–964, Colliot-Thélène, J.-L.; Parimala, R., Invent. Math. 101, no. 1, 81–99. {{mr|0419427}}

== Honors ==
On [[National Science Day]] in 2020, [[Smriti Irani]], head of the Ministry of Women and Child Development of the [[Government of India]], announced the establishment of chairs at institutes across India in the names of Raman Parimala and other ten Indian women scientists.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.shethepeople.tv/news/11-chairs-women-scientists-names|title = Science Institutes to Have 11 Chairs in Women Scientists' Names - SheThePeople TV}}</ref>
Parimala was an [[list of International Congresses of Mathematicians Plenary and Invited Speakers|invited speaker at the International Congress of Mathematicians]] in [[Zurich]] in 1994 and gave a talk [http://www.mathunion.org/ICM/ICM1994.1/Main/icm1994.1.0324.0332.ocr.pdf ''Study of quadratic forms — some connections with geometry''] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161003181416/http://www.mathunion.org/ICM/ICM1994.1/Main/icm1994.1.0324.0332.ocr.pdf |date=3 October 2016 }}. She gave a plenary address ''Arithmetic of linear algebraic groups over two dimensional fields'' at the Congress in [[Hyderabad (India)|Hyderabad]]  in 2010.

* Fellow of the [[Indian Academy of Sciences]]<ref name=":0" />
* Fellow of [[Indian National Science Academy]]<ref name=":0" />
* [[Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Award|Bhatnagar Award]] in 1987<ref name=":0" />
* Honorary Membership of the [[London Mathematical Society]] in 2024<ref name=LMS>[https://scholarblogs.emory.edu/math/38 Dr. Parimala Raman Elected to Honorary Membership of the London Mathematical Society] Emory Math News Aug 4, 2024</ref> 
* Honorary doctorate from the [[University of Lausanne]] in 1999<ref name=":0" />
* [[Srinivasa Ramanujan]] Birth Centenary Award in 2003.<ref name=":0" />
* [[TWAS Prize]] for Mathematics (2005).<ref name=":0" /><ref name="Prizes and Awards">{{Cite web |url=http://twas.org/opportunities/prizes-and-awards |title=Prizes and Awards |date=2016 |publisher=The World Academy of Sciences}}</ref>
* Fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]] (2012)<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved 2013-05-05.</ref>
